headline: MP Rumeen Farhana and OC of Sarail Police Station clash over security and corruption
summary: A heated confrontation occurred between the lawmaker and the officer-in-charge over alleged security lapses and police misconduct in Brahmanbaria.
details: A heated confrontation broke out on Thursday night between Brahmanbaria-2 MP Rumeen Farhana and the officer-in-charge (OC) of Sarail Police Station, Mohammad Monjur Kader Bhuiyan.
The lawmaker visited the station to address alleged security lapses and complaints of police misconduct, leading to a tense exchange in the OC’s office.
MP Rumeen Farhana accused the OC of behaving discourteously and alleged that he was involved in corruption, including taking money from businesses involved in sand extraction and brick kilns.
A local resident, Unda Mia, accused the OC of taking Tk 30,000 from him and alleged that police had assaulted and detained him.
The OC denied all allegations of bribery and corruption, stating he did not know the complainant and only attended official state functions.
Regarding security, the OC claimed that manpower shortages made it difficult to assign a separate police team to the MP's personal security during Durga Puja.
MP Rumeen Farhana stated that as an elected member of parliament, she is entitled to special protocol and security under the state's 'Warrant of Precedence' and 'Red Book'.
The OC further alleged that the MP arrived with a large group of people, creating a 'mob-like situation' and that she had coached the people accompanying her to make false claims.
caption:
A lawmaker and a police chief clash! MP Rumeen Farhana and the Sarail OC trade accusations of corruption and security lapses.

A heated confrontation broke out on Thursday night between Brahmanbaria-2 MP Rumeen Farhana and the officer-in-charge (OC) of Sarail Police Station, Mohammad Monjur Kader Bhuiyan.

The lawmaker visited the station to address alleged security lapses and complaints of police misconduct, leading to a tense exchange in the OC’s office.

MP Rumeen Farhana accused the OC of behaving discourteously and alleged that he was involved in corruption, including taking money from businesses involved in sand extraction and brick kilns.

A local resident, Unda Mia, accused the OC of taking Tk 30,000 from him and alleged that police had assaulted and detained him.

The OC denied all allegations of bribery and corruption, stating he did not know the complainant and only attended official state functions.

Regarding security, the OC claimed that manpower shortages made it difficult to assign a separate police team to the MP's personal security during Durga Puja.

MP Rumeen Farhana stated that as an elected member of parliament, she is entitled to special protocol and security under the state's 'Warrant of Precedence' and 'Red Book'.

The OC further alleged that the MP arrived with a large group of people, creating a 'mob-like situation' and that she had coached the people accompanying her to make false claims.

headline: 35 Bangladeshis repatriated from Italy, Greece and Cyprus
summary: The returnees arrived in Dhaka on a special chartered flight and are receiving reintegration support from BRAC and the EU.
details: Thirty-five Bangladeshis returned from Italy, Greece, and Cyprus, arriving at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka this morning on a special chartered flight.
Of the returnees, 19 were from Italy, 10 from Greece, and six from Cyprus. They arrived on flight PVG-9445 around 8:15 am.
BRAC’s Migration Programme, supported by Civil Aviation Security and the Expatriates’ Welfare Desk, provided the returnees with emergency assistance, counselling, and financial support.
Shariful Hasan, associate director of BRAC’s Migration Programme, stated that the returnees are receiving assistance under the Prottasha-2 project, funded by BRAC and the EU.
The returnees will receive training, counselling, and financial aid to help them rebuild their livelihoods and reintegrate into society.
This operation follows two other repatriations this year, with 40 people returning on August 27 and 27 people returning on May 21.
Bangladesh and the EU signed standard operating procedures in 2017 to facilitate the return of undocumented Bangladeshis from European countries.
Around 5,000 Bangladeshis have returned under this arrangement so far, with the highest numbers coming from Cyprus, Italy, Romania, and France.
